C0400.d: C0400 is publicly undocumented: none of the published J2012 lists contains it, neither does GM's PIP5094, and a search of NHTSA's bulletin index finds nothing. Only the part from the title is described here.
s: ABS, traction control and stability warning lamps on
Wheels spin freely when pulling away on slippery ground
c: Open or shorted coil of a traction control valve
Valve driver inside the brake control module failed
Poor supply or ground of the brake control module

C0401.d: There is no public evidence that any maker uses C0401. The code is missing from the publicly available J2012 lists and from GM's PIP5094; the only NHTSA index hit is a BMW program number.
s: Traction or stability control cannot be switched off or on
TCS OFF or ESP OFF lamp lit permanently
c: Button stuck pressed or contacts dirty
Open or grounded lead between button and brake module
Liquid spilled into the switch panel

C0402.d: Publicly available J2012 tables skip C0402, yet GM assigns it in its rear differential clutch control module: the 2010–11 Saab 9-5 and the 2011 9-4X call it Transfer Case Solenoid Valve and describe the rear drive clutch solenoid, which the module drives by PWM to set the clutch pressure and so the torque sent rearward; the 2008–12 Saab 9-3 XWD calls it Differential Clutch Solenoid Valve. No maker documents it as a t
s: Service Rear Axle or AWD warning displayed
Car drives on the front wheels only
c: Open or shorted solenoid valve circuit at the rear drive unit
Valve calibration not stored after module replacement
Solenoid valve sticking because of contaminated or aged clutch fluid
Corroded connector on the rear axle module

C0405.d: C0405 could not be found in any public source, including the public J2012 tables, GM's PIP5094 and NHTSA's bulletin index, and no maker publishes a time limit for a traction control intervention. So only the monitored function is outlined.
s: Traction control lamp flashes for a long time or stays on
Engine power reduced and a wheel braked without reason
Hot or smelling brake on one wheel
c: Erratic wheel speed signal faking continuous wheel spin
Spare wheel or tires of different size on one axle
Hydraulic control valve sticking in the brake unit

C0410.d: C0410 has no public trace; searches of the publicly available J2012 tables, of GM's keyword bulletin PIP5094 and of NHTSA's bulletin index came up empty. The text is therefore restricted to the sensor named in the title.
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable with a warning message
Forward collision warning or emergency braking disabled
c: Loose or corroded connector of the front radar sensor
Sensor or bracket bent after a minor impact, alignment lost

C0420.d: No public document shows a maker using C0420. It does not appear in the openly accessible J2012 lists, in GM's PIP5094 or in the NHTSA bulletin index, so only the module from the title is covered.
s: Adaptive cruise control and related assists unavailable
Driver assist warning in the instrument cluster
c: ACC module software or calibration out of date
Low or unstable supply voltage during self-test
Internal hardware fault of the ACC module

C0440.d: C0440 cannot be verified publicly; searches of the available J2012 tables, GM bulletin PIP5094 and the full NHTSA index found no hit. Its title is word for word that of C0455, which GM does use for the steering wheel position sensor read by the brake module; the description here sticks to the sensor.
s: Stability control and traction control warning lamps on
Service StabiliTrak or ESP message
c: Fretting corrosion or loose fit at the sensor connector
Zero position not calibrated after alignment or column work

C0445.d: No accessible J2012 list contains C0445, and no manufacturer bulletin or service page using it could be found, so its exact meaning cannot be proven publicly. The title points to a steering wheel position sensor whose zero point was never learned or has been lost.
s: ESC or traction control warning lamp on
Stability control unavailable
Steering wheel reading not zero when driving straight (scan tool)
c: Zero-point calibration skipped after alignment, steering work or sensor replacement
Stored calibration lost after battery disconnection or low voltage
Stability control module replaced or reprogrammed without relearning the angle

C0450.d: C0450 does not occur in the accessible J2012 lists. Its only public manufacturer use is GM: bulletin PIC5321A for the 2010–2011 Cadillac DTS links C0450 with Service Power Steering and Service Brake System messages, a lit check-engine lamp and cycling door locks, caused by an engine harness chafed through on the transmission.
s: Steering or brake system warning message in the cluster
Rear steering locked straight ahead, larger turning circle
Check-engine lamp on some GM models
c: Wiring harness chafed or pinched (GM DTS case at the transmission)
Faulty position sensor in the rear steering actuator
Corroded or loose connector on the actuator

C0455.d: C0455 is absent from the accessible J2012 lists but well documented at GM, where the electronic brake control module (EBCM) stores it for the steering wheel position sensor circuit. Bulletin PI0639C, covering 2007–2016 full-size pickups, SUVs, vans and the Colorado/Canyon, blames rising resistance between sensor and EBCM caused by fretting corrosion and a connector with too much play; it says not to replace the senso
s: Service StabiliTrak message and stability lamp on
ABS lamp may come on first
Stability control unavailable
c: Fretting corrosion and play at the sensor connector (GM PI0639C)
Steering wheel not aligned with the shaft master spline
EBCM programmed for the wrong sensor design

C0460.d: C0460 is not in the accessible J2012 lists; GM and Saab use it for the steering angle signal. On the 2016 Malibu the EBCM sets it after a brief low-voltage event, and turning lock to lock with ignition on resets the sensor (16-NA-151).
s: Traction or stability control lamp on
Reduced Steering Assist message, sometimes without actual loss of assist
Stability control switched off
c: Brief low voltage leaving the sensor uninitialised
Sensor trim error or control module software (GM 17-NA-284)
Angle offset after alignment or steering work
Steering angle sensor or column module defective

C0496.d: C0496 appears in no accessible J2012 list, and neither the NHTSA bulletin index nor the manufacturer portals checked contain it, so the code is not publicly verifiable; the established code with this title is C0196. What the title covers: a micromechanical gyro, usually combined with the lateral accelerometer and mounted near the centre of gravity.
s: Stability and traction control unavailable
ESC warning lamp on, depending on the make
c: Open circuit or short in the sensor wiring

C0497.d: Neither the accessible J2012 lists nor any manufacturer bulletin or service text mention C0497, so its use cannot be confirmed publicly. The title describes a yaw rate signal that is electrically present but does not match how the car moves.
s: ESC lamp on, stability control switched off
Unwanted brake interventions when cornering
c: Yaw rate sensor offset or drift
Sensor loose, twisted or mounted in the wrong orientation
Wrong comparison input (steering angle not calibrated, wheel speed fault)

C0498.d: C0498 is in none of the accessible J2012 lists. GM does use the number: bulletin PIP5094, a terminal-test reminder for GM cars and light trucks of 2014 and earlier, names C0498 and C0499 among many chassis codes, but without any wording, so GM's meaning stays undocumented and a lateral accelerometer fault is not confirmed; the established code with this title is C0186.
s: Stability control unavailable, ESC lamp depending on the make
Lateral acceleration reads a fixed value on the scan tool
c: Open circuit or short in the signal, reference or ground wire
Loose or corroded connector at the sensor cluster

C0499.d: C0499 is missing from the accessible J2012 lists. GM bulletin PIP5094 names C0499 next to C0498 without saying what it stands for, so no manufacturer confirms a lateral acceleration meaning; the established code with this title is C0185.
s: ESC lamp on, stability control switched off until restart
Unexpected ESC interventions on banked roads
c: Offset or drift of the lateral acceleration sensor
Sensor cluster loose or not mounted level
